page: Microsoft Azure L4s_v4 is a virtual machine instance from the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor with 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 960 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2158.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.48 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are less competitive. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 3990.37 and the uncached memory bandwidth read-only large block speed of 36.35 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with clang are relatively weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4s_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and substantial local storage capacity, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The hardware features advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations, which support average-tier performance in small-scale LLM inference. However, the low multi-core scaling and limited memory bandwidth make it less suitable for heavy multi-threaded compute, large-scale database operations, or medium-to-large LLM inference. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded applications, lightweight database operations, text processing, and static web serving.
